previous_statement: By the extended d-inclusion inequalities, ||v_n(I_n tensor A_j)||<=(1+d)||A_j|| and ||g_n(I_n tensor B_j,X)||<=d||B_j||||X||. The product bound in the extended epsilon-C*-algebra and sum_j||A_j||||B_j||=1 therefore give ||w_prime_n(X)||<=(1+epsilon)(1+d)d||X||. The involution is isometric, so the same holds for w_doubleprime_n; hence ||I_n tensor w||<=2d for d+epsilon<=1/4. Thus one may take C_w=2 uniformly in n and B.
new_statement: This estimate is self-contained. Write B as a finite direct sum of matrix algebras. In each summand M_q choose Weyl unitaries W_ab=S^a T^b. Average U^dagger tensor U over direct-sum unitaries U whose Weyl indices are independent across summands and whose summand signs are independent. Direct computation on matrix units gives the diagonal D_q=q^(-2) sum_(a,b) W_ab^dagger tensor W_ab in each diagonal block, while sign averaging kills all cross-block terms. Thus the resulting D has a representation D=sum_j A_j tensor B_j with A_j=p_j U_j^dagger, B_j=U_j, p_j>=0, sum_j p_j=1, and consequently sum_j||A_j||||B_j||=1. Now for X=[X_pq] in M_n tensor B, matrix multiplication gives [g_n(I_n tensor B_j,X)]_pq=g(B_j,X_pq), so W_prime_n(X):=sum_j v_n(I_n tensor A_j)g_n(I_n tensor B_j,X)=I_n tensor w_prime(X); taking matrix adjoints gives W_doubleprime_n=I_n tensor w_doubleprime. The operator-space block axiom gives ||I_n tensor A_j||=||A_j|| and ||I_n tensor B_j||=||B_j||. Hence the extended d-inclusion bounds and the extended epsilon-C*-algebra product bound give ||W_prime_n(X)|| <= (1+epsilon)(1+d)d sum_j||A_j||||B_j|| ||X||=(1+epsilon)(1+d)d||X||. The level-n involution is isometric, so the same estimate holds for W_doubleprime_n. Since I_n tensor w=(W_prime_n+W_doubleprime_n)/2 and d+epsilon<=1/4 implies (1+epsilon)(1+d)<=25/16<2, one obtains ||I_n tensor w||<=2d uniformly in n and B; thus C_w=2.
